newsitem.title: UK: Timothy Benn says job cut not a signal for others.
newsitem.headline: Timothy Benn says job cut not a signal for others.

text.p: Timothy Benn Publishing said on Tuesday a shock redundancy at its flagship title was not a signal that more staff would be asked to leave the company.
Staff at TBP's flagship insurance title Post Magazine were stunned when editor Stephen Womack telephoned the office from an industry conference on Friday to be told he should not come back to work.

But chairman Timothy Benn told Reuters: "The company is not in any financial difficulty, this is merely a single, structural change. We have a cumbersome editorial structure and we have decided to streamline it".
In 1993 the group said it had secured funding for acquisitions and aimed to double in size within three years with a view to stock market flotation.
However last April eight leisure and engineering titles were sold to Nexus Media Communications last April, leaving only four publications.

Benn said after the sale group editor-in-chief David Worsfold no longer had a wide brief to look after, and that Worsfold was "versatile enough" to go back to editing Post Magazine as he has done twice before.
Womack said there had been no indication that any redundancies were imminent.
"I was staggered by the news, and I am stunned and disgusted by the way it has been handled. It is completely unacceptable to have news like this broken over the 'phone," said Womack.
"Last month I was being praised for work I had done. Now, after three years of giving my all, I feel as if I have been given the sack," he said
Benn said there was absolutely no question of Mr Womack being sacked.
"If one is going to make changes they should be seen through with speed and sensible dispatch," he said.
Womack said it was too early to say whether legal action would be appropriate.
